topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic

audits.title: 1295 Virtual Fracture Clinic: An Audit of Referral Quality and Service Effectiveness
audits.standard: Glasgow virtual fracture clinic pathway: simple stable fractures discharged directly from ED with advice and telephone support
audits.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 21% of VFC referrals were simple stable fractures suitable for direct ED discharge; 22.1% of VFC first attendances discharged without change in management versus 19.4% of 529 physical fracture clinic first attendances.

audits.other_findings: Suggested closer collaboration between orthopaedics and ED to improve referral quality.
audits.citation: Beoku-Betts C, Prodromidis A, Nazar A, Sharma D, Barton S. 1295 Virtual Fracture Clinic: An Audit of Referral Quality and Service Effectiveness. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.1042.

audits.title: 377 Audit of Barts Health NHS Trust Virtual Fracture Clinic
audits.standard: BOAST 7 Fracture Clinic Services: seen in fracture clinic within 72 hours of injury
audits.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Mean injury to VFC review 2.33 days; 51% discharged after VFC review; mean VFC to face-to-face review 15.17 days; mean time to advanced imaging 30 days.

audits.other_findings: 9% of injuries did not match injury diagnosis codes; funding, staffing, A&E education and protocol updates planned with re-audit.
audits.citation: Stimler B, Banhidy N, Parducci M, Panagopoulos G. 377 Audit of Barts Health NHS Trust Virtual Fracture Clinic. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.016.

audits.title: 525 Reducing Cross-Sectional Imaging Delays from a Virtual Fracture Clinic: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: BOAST Fracture Clinic Services: timely imaging to avoid delays to surgery
audits.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Mean time from imaging request to performance 4.51 days (range 0-30); imaging delays 29.5% of time from VFC review to surgery (9 surgical patients).

audits.intervention: Interdepartmental T&O-radiology imaging pathway with priority slots for VFC patients.

cycle2.result: Mean time from request to performance 3.56 days (range 0-24); imaging delays 21.0% of time from VFC review to surgery (10 surgical patients).

audits.other_findings: Imaging delay reduced by 21.1%; sample size is imaging requests.
audits.citation: Ting A, Saltajai K, Elnawasany M, Elkewey A, Little N. 525 Reducing Cross-Sectional Imaging Delays from a Virtual Fracture Clinic: A Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.250.

audits.title: 428 An Audit of Inappropriate Referrals to the Virtual Fracture Clinic at the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital
audits.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, NHS GGC, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 80 inappropriate referrals: 52.5% injuries not requiring follow-up, 30% no identifiable fracture; 3 patients needed urgent inpatient orthopaedic assessment.

audits.intervention: Updated referral guidelines developed jointly with A&E to resolve discrepancy between A&E and orthopaedic protocols.

cycle2.result: 24 inappropriate referrals: 70.8% injuries normally discharged from A&E, 8.3% no fracture, none required inpatient assessment.

audits.other_findings: Remaining inappropriate referrals may reflect a need for reassurance or delayed uptake of the new guidelines.
audits.citation: Lawton A. 428 An Audit of Inappropriate Referrals to the Virtual Fracture Clinic at the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.219.

audits.title: A VIRTUAL FRACTURE CLINIC AUDIT: ARE WALES MATCHING THE OUTCOMES IN ENGLAND?
audits.standard: Appropriate VFC referrals, compared with established VFCs in England
audits.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (CAVUHB)

cycle1.result: Inappropriate referrals for soft tissue knee and shoulder injuries 15.1% (n=50).

cycle2.result: Average 19% improvement in referral quality; inappropriate soft tissue referrals 4.5% (n=15); fracture clinic appointments rose by 8% to 74.4% (n=247).

audits.other_findings: 64% (n=27) of radial head fractures were still seen in clinic after VFC referral; the rise in clinic appointments was mainly from nurse practitioner referrals.
audits.citation: Ramage G, Poacher A, Ramsden M, Lewis J, Robertson A, Wilson C. A VIRTUAL FRACTURE CLINIC AUDIT: ARE WALES MATCHING THE OUTCOMES IN ENGLAND?. Orthopaedic Proceedings. 2023;105-B(SUPP_4):6-6. doi:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.4.006.

audits.title: Virtual fracture clinic delivers British Orthopaedic Association compliance.
audits.standard: British Orthopaedic Association: patients referred to fracture clinic reviewed within 72 hours
audits.setting: Fracture clinic, district general hospital (Croydon Health Services NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Mean waiting time 10.7 days; 6% seen within 72 hours.

audits.intervention: Virtual fracture clinic introduced for all ED referrals to fracture clinic.

cycle2.result: All patients reviewed within 72 hours (mean 1.3 days).

audits.other_findings: Achieved with no increase in clinic capacity and negligible cost.
audits.citation: Holgate J, Kirmani S, Anand B. Virtual fracture clinic delivers British Orthopaedic Association compliance. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2017;99(1):51-54. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2016.0255. PMID: 27652791.

audits.title: An Orthopaedic Fracture Clinic Service Audit: A Complete Loop.
audits.standard: BOAST Guideline 7 (fracture clinic services), assessed with a patient questionnaire adapted from the RCSI SWOPS questionnaire; no target stated
audits.setting: Galway University Hospital fracture clinics; tertiary care hospital, consultant-led

cycle1.result: Average wait for appointment 3.55 days (85 hours); wait to see doctor in clinic 56.81 minutes; doctors rated excellent 75%; X-ray facilities inadequate 34.7%; waiting area inadequate 44.93%; overall experience excellent 50.72%.

audits.intervention: Changed fracture clinic appointment rotation, increased doctors on site, ensured patients returning from X-ray saw the same doctor, optimised follow-up X-ray process and increased waiting area seating from about 40 to 50; findings on X-ray location passed to management.

cycle2.result: Average wait for appointment 3.21 days (77.04 hours); wait to see doctor 52.55 minutes; doctors rated excellent 73.9%; X-ray facilities inadequate 32.79%; waiting area inadequate 41.49%; overall experience excellent 53.55%.

audits.other_findings: The X-ray department remained a five-minute, partly outdoor walk from the clinic and waiting area ratings stayed poor; the year of data collection is not stated.
audits.citation: Baig MN, Ni Bhroin O, Auckloo R, Mac Dhaibheid C, Baig U, Byrne F. An Orthopaedic Fracture Clinic Service Audit: A Complete Loop. Cureus. 2017;9(11):e1890. doi:10.7759/cureus.1890. PMID: 29392102.

audits.title: The success of virtual clinics during COVID-19: A closed loop audit of the British orthopaedic association (BOAST) guidelines of outpatient orthopaedic fracture management.
audits.standard: BOAST COVID-19 guidance points 7–10: removable casts/splints in 100%; index fracture clinic appointments 100% virtually screened; follow-up by phone/video in 100%; follow-up radiographs for union in 0% (exceptions if documented)
audits.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon; 480-bed district general hospital fracture clinic and virtual fracture clinic during COVID-19

cycle1.result: 100% removable casts; 96% virtually assessed or approved for face-to-face (197 VFC, 18 approved, 8 no approval); 97% virtual follow-up or documented reason (6/223, 2.7% without); 0.4% inappropriate radiographs for union.

audits.intervention: All patients required a consultant-level senior opinion (trauma meeting, on-call consultant or VFC) before a face-to-face appointment, from 11 May 2020; email reminder to use virtual clinics.

cycle2.result: 100% removable casts; 99% virtually assessed or consultant-approved (130 VFC, 14 approved, 1 unapproved); 100% virtual follow-up or documented reason; 0.7% inappropriate radiographs for union.

audits.other_findings: A simulated virtual clinic for the 26 patients first seen face to face showed 22 appointments and 13 X-ray attendances could have been saved. The one unapproved re-audit patient was a GP referral, so GP and outside referrals are now discussed with the VFC team.
audits.citation: Dunkerley S, Kurar L, Butler K, James M, Lowdon I. The success of virtual clinics during COVID-19: A closed loop audit of the British orthopaedic association (BOAST) guidelines of outpatient orthopaedic fracture management. Injury. 2020;51(12):2822-2826. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2020.09.012. PMID: 32951919.

audits.title: Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center.
audits.standard: Predefined standards from national coronavirus outpatient guidelines and local consensus: (1) all eligible ED trauma patients referred for VFC review; (2) all patients contacted after VFC review; (3) patient-initiated follow-up by default where possible; (4) follow-up by telephone or video where possible. Target 100% for standard 1.
audits.setting: OLVG, a level 2 trauma centre and teaching hospital in Amsterdam (emergency department and virtual fracture clinic)

cycle1.result: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).

audits.intervention: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.

cycle2.result: 302/305 (98.4%) referred for VFC review; 99.0% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.0%, not reached); 41/302 (13.6%) discharged 'virtually'; 179/436 (41.1%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 98 minutes (−33 minutes vs baseline, p=0.001); time to review 47 minutes (p<0.001); time for review 35 minutes vs 45 minutes (p=0.019).

audits.other_findings: An ED orthopaedic trauma fast-track pathway was introduced alongside the VFC; 88% and 92% of suspected fracture patients were treated in fast-track rooms. Median VFC review time was 9 minutes then 7 minutes per patient.
audits.citation: Geerdink TH, Salentijn DA, de Vries KA, Noordman PCW, van Dongen JM, Haverlag R, et al.. Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center. Trauma Surg Acute Care Open. 2021;6(1):e000691. doi:10.1136/tsaco-2021-000691. PMID: 34632079.

audits.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Implementation and Adoption of a Virtual Fracture Clinic Pathway: A Closed Loop Audit.
audits.standard: Three modified BOASTs: early senior review (BOAST: new fracture clinic within 72 hours; measured as VFC review within 24 hours), minimising outpatient visits, and patient-initiated follow-up as the default; no target stated
audits.setting: University teaching hospital and regional trauma and orthopaedic referral centre serving four peripheral sites (Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda, per affiliation); non-operative fracture pathway

cycle1.result: 39% of non-operative patients triaged to the VFC within 24 hours; 61% sent directly to face-to-face clinic. 35,399 face-to-face fracture clinic appointments (also given as 35,339 in the results).

audits.intervention: COVID-19-era policy changes: mandatory VFC triage of all non-operative injuries via a smartphone referral app with daily consultant-led multidisciplinary review, and an early appropriate discharge / patient-initiated follow-up policy; national lockdowns also occurred.

cycle2.result: 100% of non-operative patients assessed in the VFC within 24 hours. Face-to-face appointments fell to 17,639, a 50.2% reduction: 3.7% attributed to national lockdowns, 14.7% to VFC triage and 35.5% to early appropriate discharge.

audits.other_findings: Sample sizes are total orthopaedic referrals in each period. Patient safety and satisfaction were not assessed.
audits.citation: Gibbons DS, Glynn AA. Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Implementation and Adoption of a Virtual Fracture Clinic Pathway: A Closed Loop Audit. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e76317. doi:10.7759/cureus.76317. PMID: 39720771.

audits.title: Audit of upper limb fracture management in an accident and emergency department.
audits.standard: Standard of treatment as determined by fracture clinic doctors; upper limb fracture treatment and referral guidelines
audits.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, Kings College Hospital, London (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Some error in 69/215 (32.1%) referrals; 51/215 (23.7%) potentially liable to increased morbidity

audits.intervention: Introduction of fracture treatment and referral guidelines in the A&E department

cycle2.result: Errors in 14/111 (12.6%); 8 patients (7.2%) at risk of increased morbidity

audits.other_findings: Overall improvement 19.5% (95% CI 12.3 to 29.7%); 16.5% (95% CI 9.1 to 23.9%) reduction in potentially more significant errors.
audits.citation: Jenkins DP, Cooke MW, Glucksman EE. Audit of upper limb fracture management in an accident and emergency department. J Accid Emerg Med. 1994;11(2):105-108. doi:10.1136/emj.11.2.105. PMID: 7921563.
